title: Introduce declarative ci-manifests and deterministic dependency snapshots
author: Maya Chen
commits: feat(ci): add declarative ci-manifests and manifest loader
feat(dep): introduce dep-snapshots/lock export and verifier
refactor(ci): convert existing workflows to manifest-driven templates
chore: remove legacy .github/workflows/* files and add migration notes
test(ci): add unit tests for manifest validator and matrix sampler
description:
Context and motivation:
We maintain a large surface of ad-hoc GitHub Actions and bespoke CI scripts. Over time this has caused inconsistent presubmit coverage, duplicated matrix definitions, and surprising test surface drift when transitive devdeps change. This PR introduces two complementary ideas to make CI more deterministic and easier to reason about: (1) declarative CI manifests that drive a small, single manifest-runner workflow; and (2) deterministic dependency snapshots that capture the full dev dependency graph for reproducible CI images and staged caching.

What this changes (high level):
- Add .github/ci-manifests/*.yml: human-friendly stage manifests that declare lanes (fastpath, full, nightly), shards, and stage-affinity. The manifest-runner compiles these into lightweight workflow inputs and keeps a single canonical workflow to execute them.
- Add tools/ci/manifest-loader.go and a small manifest-validator in tools/ci/manifest-validator/ to ensure manifests conform to schema on PRs. Validator runs in CI as a pre-merge gate.
- Add a matrix-sampler that produces reproducible test partitions given a seed + manifest; this reduces noise caused by file-ordering and gives consistent shard assignments across runs.
- Introduce dep-snapshot exporter (tools/dep-snapshot/exporter.py) that emits dep-snapshots/redwood-lock-YYYY-MM-DD.json. Snapshots include top-level devdeps, transitive resolution metadata and a checksum. CI uses the snapshot to pin bootstrap images/cache keys and to fail fast when snapshot drift is detected.
- Remove several legacy workflows and consolidate their logic into the manifest-driven runner; add a migration script scripts/prune-orphan-workflows.sh for safety.
- Add docs and a migration guide to help teams convert language-specific workflows to manifests.

Why this approach:
- Declarative manifests separate intent (what should run) from execution (how it runs), enabling a single test executor implementation to harden retries, reporting and cost-aware routing.
- Deterministic dep snapshots reduce surprise rebuilds and make cache keys stable across the fleet.
- The matrix-sampler reduces flakiness from non-deterministic test-partitioning and allows reproducible reruns of a failing shard.

Checklist implemented (tests / rollout):
- [x] Manifest schemas and validator unit tests (ci/manifest-validator/*)
- [x] Matrix sampler tests and deterministic sampling integration test
- [x] Dep snapshot exporter with CI job that uploads snapshots to artifacts
- [x] Migration notes and pruning script for legacy workflows
- [x] Docs for contributors and platform owners

Testing and CI behavior notes:
- The first CI run after merge will generate a baseline dep snapshot under dep-snapshots/ with the commit hash and author timestamp. The manifest-validator job will compare PR-modified manifests against the schema and run a lightweight dry-run (no external network).
- We kept the previous workflow interface backwards-compatible for 2 weeks using a feature flag (env CI_MANIFEST_MODE=compat) to reduce risk for active rollouts. Feature flag removed in this PR by defaulting to manifest mode.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Rollout: merge to main, monitor ci/manifest-runner job for 48 hours for increase in failures or unexpected runtime. Watch premerge latency and cache hit rates.
- Rollback: a one-line revert to restore legacy workflows exists (scripts/prune-orphan-workflows.sh --restore). If dep-snapshot drift causes failures, the CI job will reject new merges until snapshot is updated and approved by platform-oncall.

Release notes:
Introduce declarative CI manifests and deterministic dependency snapshots; consolidate legacy workflows behind a single manifest-runner; add validator and sampler to reduce flakiness and make CI caching deterministic.

Related work:
- ENG-1904: CI stability epic (matrix sampling + manifestization)
- ENG-1918: dep hygiene and lock snapshotting

Special notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on manifest schema and validator error cases (tools/ci/manifest-validator). The exporter is intentionally conservative: it emits a checksum and a resolved-ids list to make snapshot diffs small and auditable.
- I've kept per-language adapters minimal; we will follow up with a second PR to convert the TS and Go pipelines incrementally.
review_comments: Jared Lin: Left a couple of nits on manifest schema (stage 'priority' should be enum not int) and asked for clearer error messages from the validator when fields are missing.

Maya (author): Addressed the schema nit, added enumerations for priority and tightened the validator tests to include malformed manifests. Pushed one additional commit to improve validator error strings.
Priya Nair: Asked for more telemetry — specifically a metric for 'manifest_compile_duration_seconds' and a gauge for 'dep_snapshot_version'.
Maya (author): Added metrics in manifest-runner and the dep snapshot uploader, included them in docs and CI dashboards. PTAL.
Tomás Alvarez: Verified matrix-sampler determinism across 50 seeds and requested an integration test to lock behavior. Added tests/integration/ci-manifests-integration.yaml for that purpose.
Jared Lin: Approved after verifying validator tests and a successful smoke run on the manifest-runner workflow.
CI Bot: Initial run failed due to missing linter rule in tools/ci/manifest-loader.go. Author fixed by formatting with gofmt and updating makefile target. Final CI: pass.
release_notes: Platform: Declarative CI manifests and deterministic dependency snapshots. Consolidated legacy workflows into a single manifest-driven runner; introduced validator, matrix-sampler, and dep-snapshot exporter to reduce test flakiness and make cache keys stable. See docs/ci/how-ci-manifests-work.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Watch: ci.manifests.compile.time, ci.dep_snapshot.version (artifact existence), ci.matrix_sampler.reproducible_failures counter. If snapshot drift blocks merges, platform oncall can update dep-snapshots/* with signed approval.
testing_instructions: Run ./tools/ci/manifest-validator --path=.github/ci-manifests to validate. To generate a snapshot locally run python tools/dep-snapshot/exporter.py --out dep-snapshots/redwood-lock-local.json. Use `make ci-runner` to execute the manifest-runner in a containerized dev loop.
